label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court event window object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function. The same name is used on other types to pass the object on to another function, but that is only a hint.

label: Court event items
summary: The list of court events shown in the court event window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model (the list a widget repeats over) in the royal court window, one row per event. The game does not name the item type.

label: Event window insert
summary: Going by its name, the part of the court event window that shows an event; it can tell whether an event is open.
details: Vanilla reads `.HasOpenEvent` on it to switch other widgets off while an event is open, and also uses it as the data context of a widget. The game does not name its type.

label: Royal court window
summary: Going by its name, the royal court window this court event window belongs to.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Similar names on other window types are used to reach the royal court window and read its tab or character, which is only a hint.

label: Has open event
summary: Whether a court event is currently open in the window.
details: Going by its name and the boolean result. Vanilla uses the same name on the event window insert to show or hide widgets.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the court event window is currently shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of a part of the royal court window.

label: Open event
summary: Opens the given court event in the court event window.
details: It takes one argument. Vanilla calls it when a court event item is clicked and passes that item.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a court event item, such as the clicked item

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, the court event window itself.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other types use `.Self` to hand an object to another function, for example `Character.Self`, which is only a hint.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court grandeur data object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: Baseline grandeur
summary: The baseline court grandeur, the value the current grandeur drifts towards.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it as the "Baseline" in the grandeur tooltip and as a value in the court amenities window.

label: Change towards baseline
summary: How much the court grandeur changes each month on its way towards the baseline.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it with a "/month" unit and only shows a widget when it is not zero.

label: Current grandeur
summary: The court's current grandeur value.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it in the grandeur tooltip header and compares it with the baseline.

label: Current grandeur level
summary: The court's current grandeur level, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the "Grandeur Level" title and passes it on to look up the modifier of that level.

label: Grandeur level without grace
summary: The court's grandeur level when the grace period is ignored.
details: After losing a level the court keeps its effects for a while (the grace period). This gives the level it will fall to once that ends. Vanilla uses it in the grace period tooltips.

label: Days until baseline
summary: The number of days until the court's grandeur reaches the baseline.
details: Vanilla shows it as a time span ("Baseline will be reached in ...") and shows a widget only when it is not zero.

label: Level difference from expected
summary: How many levels the court's grandeur is away from the expected level.
details: A whole number. Vanilla shows it, and its absolute value, in the tooltip that says whether the court is above or below expectation.

label: Grace period end date
summary: The date on which the court's grace period ends.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla reads `.GetTimeToDate` and `.GetTimeDiffFromNow` on it to show how long is left.

label: Minimum expected grandeur
summary: Going by its name, the lowest grandeur value the court is expected to have.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Minimum expected level
summary: The lowest grandeur level the court is expected to have.
details: A whole number. Vanilla subtracts it from the current level to say how far the court is above or below expectation.

label: This grandeur data
summary: Going by its name, the court grandeur data object itself.
details: Vanilla only uses it in a commented-out line, as a data context. Other types use `.Self` to hand an object to another function.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court grandeur level object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: Grandeur needed
summary: The amount of grandeur a court needs to reach this level.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it as "requires N+ court grandeur" and in the warning that a level is not kept.

label: Level number
summary: The number of this grandeur level.
details: A whole number. Vanilla shows it in the "Grandeur Level" title and passes it on to get the effects of that level.

label: This level
summary: Going by its name, the grandeur level object itself.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other types use `.Self` to hand an object to another function, which is only a hint.

label: Should show
summary: Whether this grandeur level should be displayed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of the level entries in the court amenities window.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court grandeur window object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: Baseline breakdown tooltip
summary: The tooltip content that breaks down where the baseline grandeur comes from.
details: Going by its name and its use as the data context of tooltip widgets in the court amenities window. The game does not name its type.

label: Change breakdown tooltip
summary: The tooltip content that breaks down the monthly change of grandeur towards the baseline.
details: Going by its name and its use as a data context in the court amenities window. The game does not name its type.

label: Grandeur levels
summary: The list of grandeur levels shown in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model (the list a widget repeats over) in the court amenities window, one row per level. The game does not name the item type.

label: Level effects text
summary: The text that describes the effects of one grandeur level.
details: Vanilla passes a level number and puts the text under "Effects" in the level tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, such as a level's value

label: Total level effects text
summary: The text that describes the effects of a grandeur level, apparently adding up the levels below it.
details: The "cumulative" in the name suggests the effects add up; the game says nothing more. Vanilla passes the current level in the tooltip of the court's present level.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, such as the current level

label: Royal court window
summary: Going by its name, the royal court window this grandeur window belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads `.GetCharacter` on it and uses the result as a data context. The game does not name its type.

label: World rank
summary: The court's rank in the world, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the text "Ranked N in the World".

label: World rank tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the court's world rank.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the court amenities window.

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, the court grandeur window itself.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other types use `.Self` to hand an object to another function, which is only a hint.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court position object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: AI candidate score
summary: The AI's score for the candidate of this court position, as text.

summary: The task the holder of this court position is currently performing.

label: Aptitude
summary: Going by its name, the aptitude of the court position's holder.

summary: The aptitude of the position's holder, written as text.

label: Aptitude tooltip
summary: The tooltip content that explains the aptitude of the position's holder.

label: Description
summary: The description text of this court position.

label: Employee
summary: The character who holds this court position.

label: Employee bonuses text
summary: The text that lists the bonuses the position gives to its holder.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla shows it in a shared tooltip layout.

label: Employee salary breakdown
summary: The tooltip text that breaks down the salary of the position's holder.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Employee salary text
summary: The salary of the position's holder, written as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Employee salary, short
summary: The salary of the position's holder, in a short text form.
details: Vanilla uses it in a short localization line in the court positions window.

label: Employer
summary: The character who employs the holder of this court position.
details: The game says it returns a character. Vanilla reads its name and uses it as the data context of tooltip widgets.

label: Employer bonuses text
summary: The text that lists the bonuses the position gives to the employer.
details: Vanilla shows it in the appoint window, the court positions window and the great steppe window.

label: Employer court bonuses text
summary: The text that lists the bonuses the position gives to the employer's court.
details: Vanilla uses it under the heading "Effects on" the court owner's court or realm.

label: Employer salary breakdown
summary: The tooltip text that breaks down the salary the employer pays.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the appoint window, the court positions window and the great steppe window.

label: Employer salary text
summary: The salary the employer pays, written as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Monthly Salary" when replacing the current holder.

label: Employer salary, short
summary: The salary the employer pays, in a short text form.
details: Vanilla uses it in a short localization line in the court positions window.

label: Task validity text
summary: Going by its name, the text that says whether the given task is valid for this position.
details: It takes one argument, probably a task. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the task to describe.

label: Court position name
summary: The name of a court position, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in relation texts, followed by the position type's icon, also after the liege's name ('[liege's] [position] [icon]').

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of this court position, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in sentences such as "Currently appointed ...".

label: On revoke description
summary: Going by its name, the text that describes what happens when the position is revoked.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Opinion bonus
summary: The opinion bonus tied to this court position, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign in the line "Opinion Bonus". The game does not say who gets the opinion of whom.

label: Position type
summary: The kind of court position this is.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla reads its name and uses it as a data context in the court positions window.

label: Revoke cost text
summary: The cost of revoking the position, written as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the line "Cost you:" of a tooltip.

label: Task tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text of the given task of this position.
details: It takes one argument, probably a task. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the task.

label: Time of service
summary: How long the holder has served in this position, as text.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla shows it in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Has active task
summary: Whether the position's holder is performing a task.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visibility condition in the shared tooltip layout.

label: Is active task
summary: Whether the given task is the one the holder is performing.
details: Vanilla passes the task type of a row and shows the "deactivate" or "activate" text accordingly.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether this court position is valid.
details: Vanilla shows the position's own name and description when it is valid, and a text worked out for the character when it is not. The game does not say more about what valid means.

label: Is valid task
summary: Going by its name, whether the given task is valid for this position.
details: It takes one argument, probably a task. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the task to check.

label: Make scope
summary: Going by its name, makes a script scope out of the court position.
details: The game says it returns a scope. Vanilla does not use it on this type. Other types use `.MakeScope` the same way, for example `GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue(...)`, which is only a hint.

label: Open replace window
summary: Opens the window for replacing the holder of this position.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click in the court positions window.

label: Open revoke confirmation
summary: Opens the window that asks to confirm revoking the position.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click in the court positions window.

label: This position
summary: The court position itself, to hand it to another function.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla passes it to task functions that need the position, for example to describe the effects of a task.

label: Stop task command
summary: Going by its name, a command that stops the given task of this position.
details: It returns a command object that can be sent to the game. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Going by the name, the task to stop.

label: Toggle task command
summary: A command that switches the given task of this position on or off.
details: It returns a command object. Vanilla uses it to get the button text, and to show and enable the button only when the command is valid.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the court position item object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: Can hire position
summary: Going by its name, whether a holder can be hired for this position.
details: Vanilla does not use it on this type. The same name is used on the position type with a character as argument, which is only a hint.

label: Background
summary: The background image of this position's row.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla uses it as the texture of a widget in the court positions window.

label: Best candidate AI score
summary: The AI score of the best candidate for this position.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it as "Can AI: ..." in the court positions window.

label: Best candidate score text
summary: Going by its name, a text that describes the best candidate's AI score.
details: Vanilla does not use it.

label: Court owner
summary: The owner of the court this position belongs to.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla uses it as the data context of widgets in the court positions window.

label: Item id
summary: An identifier text of this row, used as a key.
details: Vanilla uses it as the name of a variable in the interface's variable system, to switch a state on and off and to check it.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the position of this row, as plain text without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a widget in the court positions window.

label: Hired courtiers
summary: Going by its name, how many courtiers are hired in this position.
details: A whole number. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Portrait animation
summary: The animated portrait texture for this row, drawn in a given environment and camera.

summary: The court position this row stands for.

label: Position AI score
summary: The AI score of this position.
details: Returns a number with decimals. Vanilla shows it as "Pos AI: ..." in the court positions window.

label: Requirements tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that lists what is required for this position.

label: Tasks
summary: The list of tasks of this position.

label: Position type
summary: The kind of court position of this row.

label: Has valid courtiers

label: Is allowed

label: Is employed

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether the position's row is enabled.

label: Open appoint window
summary: Going by its name, opens the window for appointing someone to this position.

label: This item
summary: Going by its name, the court position item itself.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the task item object itself.
details: The game gives no return type and vanilla never uses this exact function.

label: Court position
summary: The court position this task row belongs to.
details: The game does not name the return type. Vanilla uses it as a data context in the court positions window.

label: Task
summary: The task this row stands for.

label: Is active
summary: Going by its name, whether this task is currently running.

label: Is shown
summary: Whether this task row is shown.

label: This task item
summary: Going by its name, the task item itself.

label: Access itself
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the task type object itself.

label: Description
summary: The description text of this court position task.
